question: About what fraction of hospital waste is actually hazardous?
explanation: Most hospital waste is regular trash! Only a small fraction (about 10 to 25 percent) is dangerous and needs special handling.

question: Why do we need to manage hospital waste carefully?

options.A: To maintain a pleasant smell throughout the hospital wards
options.B: To reduce the overall cost of hospital administrative duties
options.C: To ensure that all medical supplies are completely recycled
options.D: To prevent infections, toxic injuries, and sharp punctures

explanation: Hazardous waste carries germs and dangerous materials that can easily hurt patients, hospital staff, and the public if we aren't careful.

question: Which of these items goes into the sharps container?
explanation: Sharps are anything that can cut or poke your skin, like needles, blades, and broken glass. Always drop them straight into a puncture-proof box!

question: What makes pathological waste different from normal trash?

options.A: Pathological waste is generated exclusively in hospital kitchens.
options.B: Pathological waste consists of recognizable human tissues and body parts.
options.C: Pathological waste includes only broken glass and empty medicine vials.
options.D: Pathological waste is composed strictly of administrative paper records.

explanation: Pathological waste refers to body tissues and parts. Because of what they are, they need special, respectful handling and high-heat burning.

question: Why should you sort waste right at the bedside or where it is generated?

options.A: To speed up the physical transport of bins to the incinerator
options.B: To prevent hazardous waste from contaminating general trash
options.C: To reduce the number of waste bins needed in each ward
options.D: To make it easier for patients to clean up their bedside

explanation: Sorting waste immediately stops dangerous items from mixing with safe rubbish. It keeps disposal safe and easy for everyone!

question: Why is it a bad idea to sort mixed waste later in the utility room?

options.A: It greatly increases the risk of accidental needlestick injuries.
options.B: It causes color-coded bags to fade under fluorescent lights.
options.C: It makes the municipal waste collectors charge extra fees.
options.D: It takes too much time away from cleaning patient rooms.

explanation: Never rummage through bags of unsorted waste! You might accidentally poke yourself on a hidden needle or touch dangerous fluids.

question: When should you tie up and replace a medical waste bag?
explanation: Always tie bags when they are about 3/4 full. This leaves enough space to close them securely without tearing the plastic.

question: What is the safest way to carry a full medical waste bag?

options.A: Drag it across the floor to avoid straining your back muscles
options.B: Hug it tightly against the chest to balance the heavy weight
options.C: Lift it by the neck and keep it away from the body
options.D: Balance it on the shoulder while walking to the disposal site

explanation: Hold the bag by its neck away from your body. That way, if a hidden needle pokes through the plastic, it won't hit you!

question: Which machine uses high-pressure steam to sterilize medical items?
explanation: An autoclave uses hot, pressurized steam to kill germs on equipment and medical waste effectively.

question: Why do we use an incinerator (high heat) for body parts and tissues?

options.A: It operates at room temperature without requiring any fuel source.
options.B: It completely destroys anatomical material down to ash at very high heat.
options.C: It turns body tissues into recyclable plastic polymers for industry.
options.D: It is the only method that does not produce any smoke or gas emissions.

explanation: Incineration uses extreme heat to safely and completely turn anatomical waste into ash, which is important for health and safety reasons.

question: Where should the toxic ash from burning medical waste be dumped?

options.A: Shallow trenches dug right behind the hospital
options.B: Open community rubbish pits near local farms
options.C: Secure engineered landfills with protective liners
options.D: Standard municipal recycling bins for plastic

explanation: Incinerator ash has chemicals and toxins in it, so it must go into a specially lined landfill to protect our soil and drinking water.

question: What is the main danger of dumping and burning medical waste out in the open?

options.A: It pollutes the air and spreads dangerous pathogens into soil and water
options.B: It wastes valuable electrical energy that the hospital could have used
options.C: It makes the municipal waste collectors take much longer to finish routes
options.D: It causes local hospital linen to become stained with dark soot

explanation: Open burning creates toxic smoke, and dumping waste outside leaves germs out in the open where they can infect people and water sources.

question: What is the very first thing you should do if you accidentally poke yourself with a used needle?

options.A: Wrap the finger tightly in adhesive tape and keep working
options.B: Apply a tight tourniquet around the entire upper arm
options.C: Wash the wound immediately with soap and running water
options.D: Soak the hand in a strong chlorine bleach solution

explanation: Don't panic! Immediately wash the spot with soap and clean running water, then report the incident right away for proper care.

question: Which of these actions is NOT safe when handling medical waste?

options.A: Washing puncture wounds immediately and reporting the incident
options.B: Receiving the hepatitis B vaccination before working in clinical units
options.C: Recapping used hypodermic needles with both hands before disposal
options.D: Wearing heavy-duty utility gloves when cleaning up waste storage areas

explanation: Never try to recap a used needle with both hands—that's one of the quickest ways to get a accidental needlestick injury!
